label: Person
name: Antiochus Chuzon
summary:
Antiochus Chuzon, praetorian prefect of the East and consul, was a high official of the Eastern Roman Empire who played a key role in the compilation of the Codex Theodosianus. Born into a prominent family, he rose to prominence under Emperor Valentinian II, becoming one of the most influential figures in the empire's governance.

As praetorian prefect, Chuzon oversaw the administration of the eastern provinces, including the crucial territories along the Euphrates River. His efforts to reform the empire's tax system and promote trade helped stabilize the region, making him a favorite among the Roman people.

Chuzon's legacy extends beyond his administrative achievements, as he was also a key figure in the early Christian Church. He is said to have personally sponsored the construction of several churches in Antioch, cementing the city's status as a major center of Christianity.

In the end, Chuzon's remarkable life came to an abrupt close with his death in 500 CE, leaving behind a lasting impact on the Eastern Roman Empire and the early Christian Church.
